project_overview: This Vue.js application appears to be a web portal for educational services, potentially related to course enrollment, exam management, and student results. The structure consists of several Vue components, likely representing different user interface pages and associated logic. The dependency graph reveals significant navigation routes and component interactions. The confirmed issue summary highlights accessibility and performance concerns across several key components.

layers.description: User interface components and Vue files responsible for rendering the application.

macro_trends.title: Potential UI/Accessibility Fragility
macro_trends.description: Multiple files (ExamFormSubmission, iLikeCoursesNew, SelectedApplicationService, Transactions) exhibit multiple UI/Accessibility issues, suggesting potential inconsistencies in styling and accessibility implementation. Addressing these could significantly improve the user experience and ensure compliance with accessibility standards.

macro_trends.title: Route Navigation Over-Reliance
macro_trends.description: The heavy reliance on Router push navigations in several components (ApplicationServices, Transactions, iLikeCoursesNew) could introduce tight coupling and make the application more difficult to maintain and test.  Consider alternative navigation strategies where appropriate.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow begins with the ExamFormSubmission component, processes data, and potentially interacts with the Transactions component for recording the submission.  Further investigation is needed to understand the complete data flow and potential points of failure.

key_workflows.name: User Result Retrieval
key_workflows.description: The ResultPage component, likely consuming data from other components or services, represents a critical workflow for displaying student results.  Performance and accessibility within this workflow require careful scrutiny.
